description:
The surah that opens with the oath of the Divine One swearing by the angels arrayed before Him in devotional ranks, **The Ranged Ones**—thereafter, by other angels propelling the clouds, dispelling evil, and reciting God's praise. It takes its name from verse 1, which refers to a gropu of angels as "those ranged (ṣāffāt) in ranks". The central point of this surah is the unity of God (verse 4 and verse 180 ff.) and the refutation of the pagan belief that the angels were daughters of God and worthy of worship. The angels themselves are quoted to refute this (verse 164 ff.). The prophethood of Muḥammad, is affirmed, as is the Hereafter. There are two supporting sections: the scenes in the Hereafter (verse 19 ff.) and the stories of earlier prophets (verse 75 ff.).
The surah is also known as Devotional Ranks, Drawn Up In Ranks, Ranged in Order, Ranged in Rows, The Rangers, The Ranks, Those Ranged in Ranks, Those in Ranks, Who Stand Arrayed in Rows

2.1: Or 'hold back forcibly,' or 'scold severely.' Said to refer to angels who drive the clouds, or hold back (or drive away) the eavesdropping devils, or to angels (or verses of the Qur'ān) that restrain people from sins.

3.1: That is, the faithful, or the angels, who recite the Qur'ān or the scriptures.

5.1: That is, the points of sunrise at the winter and summer solstices. Cf. <{["Q", "7:137"]}>; <{["Q", "55:17"]}>; <{["Q", "70:40"]}>.

6.1: Or 'the heaven of the earth,' or 'the nearest heaven.'
6.2: Or 'We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment, the stars.'

10.1: That is, of celestial intelligence. See Ṭabarī for several related traditions from the Prophet (_ṣ_).

11.1: Or 'more tough' (or strong), or 'more difficult.' Cf. <{["Q", "79:27"]}>.

54.1: That is, one of his companions in paradise.

65.1: 'The devil's head' is either a purely imaginative metaphor, or a simile that likens the spathes of the Zaqqūm tree to that of an Arabian plant by this name, or to certain rocks to be found around the city of Makkah which were called 'the devils' heads' because of their hideous appearance.

88.1: Or 'threw a look at the stars.'

101.1: That is, Ishmael, who was Abraham's first born. That it was Ishmael to whom the following episode of the sacrifice pertains is also supported by the fact that verses pertaining to the birth of Isaac follow the account of Ishmael's sacrifice.

130.1: In accordance with an alternate reading (_salāmun ʿalā Āl-i Yā Sīn_), narrated from Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, Yaʿqūb, Ruways, al-Aʿraj, Shaybah, Zayd ibn ʿAlī and others (see _Muʿjam al-Qirā'āt al-Qur'āniyyah_, vol. 5, p. 246), the translation will be 'Peace be upon the progeny of Yā Sīn' (i.e. the Prophet, who is referred to as Yā Sīn in <{["Q", "36:1"]}>). Traditions narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās (_al-Durr al-Manthūr_, vol. 5, p. 286), Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq (_Maʿānī al-Akhbār_, p. 122) and Imam ʿAlī ibn Mūsā al-Riḍā (_ʿUyūn Akhbār al-Riḍā_, vol. 1, p.237) also support this reading.

156.1: That is, in support of what they assert.

164.1: Verses <{["Q", "37:164"]}> - <{["Q", "37:166"]}> quote the words of the angels referred to in verse <{["Q", "37:1"]}>.

167.1: That is, the pagans of Makkah.

translations.2: by the ones who drive vigorously,<{["F", 1]}>
translations.3: by the ones who recite the reminder:<{["F", 1]}>
translations.4: indeed your God is certainly One,
translations.5: the Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and the Lord of the easts.<{["F", 1]}>
translations.6: Indeed We have adorned the lowest heaven<{["F", 1]}> with the finery of the stars,<{["F", 2]}>
translations.7: and to guard from any froward devil.
translations.8: They do not eavesdrop on the Supernal Elite but are shot at from every side,
translations.9: to drive them away, and for them there is a constant mortification,
translations.10: except him who snatches a snatch,<{["F", 1]}> whereat there pursues him a piercing flame.<{["F", 2]}>
translations.11: _Ask_ them, is their creation more prodigious<{["F", 1]}> or [that of other creatures] that We have created? Indeed We created them from a viscous clay.
translations.12: Indeed _you_ wonder, while they engage in ridicule,
translations.13: and [even] when admonished do not take admonition,
translations.14: and when they see a sign they make it an object of ridicule,
translations.15: and say, 'This is nothing but plain magic!'
translations.16: 'What! When we are dead and have become dust and bones, shall we be resurrected?
translations.18: _Say_, 'Yes! And you will be utterly humble.'
translations.19: It will be only a single shout and, behold, they will look on,
translations.20: and say, 'Woe to us! This is the Day of Retribution!'
translations.21: 'This is the Day of Judgement that you used to deny!'
translations.22: 'Muster the wrongdoers and their mates<{["F", 1]}> and what they used to worship
translations.23: besides Allah, and show them the way to hell!
translations.24: [But first] stop them! For they must be questioned.'
translations.25: 'Why is it that you do not support<{["F", 1]}> one another [today]?'
translations.26: Rather today they are [meek and] submissive!
translations.27: Some of them will turn to others, questioning each other.
translations.28: They will say, 'Indeed you used to accost us peremptorily.'<{["F", 1]}>
translations.29: They will answer, 'Rather you [yourselves] had no faith.
translations.30: We had no authority over you. Rather you [yourselves] were a rebellious lot.
translations.31: So our Lord's word became due against us that we shall indeed taste [the punishment].
translations.32: So we perverted you, for we were perverse [ourselves].'
translations.33: So that day they will share in the punishment.
translations.34: Indeed that is how We deal with the guilty.
translations.35: Indeed it was they who, when they were told, 'There is no god except Allah,' used to be disdainful,
translations.36: and [they would] say, 'Shall we abandon our gods for a crazy poet?'
translations.37: Rather he has brought [them] the truth, and confirmed the [earlier] apostles.
translations.38: Indeed you will taste the painful punishment,
translations.39: and you will be requited only for what you used to do
translations.41: For such there is a known<{["F", 1]}> provision
translations.42: —fruits—and they will be held in honour,
translations.45: served around with a cup from a clear fountain,
translations.47: wherein there will be neither headache nor will it cause them stupefaction,
translations.48: and with them will be maidens of restrained glances with big [beautiful] eyes,
translations.49: as if they were hidden<{["F", 1]}> ostrich eggs.
translations.50: Some of them will turn to others, questioning each other.
translations.51: One of them will say, 'Indeed I had a companion
translations.52: who used to say, "Are you really among those who affirm
translations.53: [that] when we are dead and have become dust and bones, we shall indeed be brought to retribution?" '
translations.54: He<{["F", 1]}> will say, 'Will you have a look?'
translations.55: Then he will take a look and sight him in the middle of hell.
translations.56: He will say, 'By Allah, you had almost ruined me!
translations.57: And had it not been for my Lord's blessing, I too would have been among the arraigned!'
translations.58: 'Is it [true] that we shall not die [anymore],
translations.59: aside from our first death, and that we shall not be punished?
translations.60: This is indeed the great success!
translations.61: Let all the workers work for the like of this!'
translations.62: Is this a better hospitality, or the Zaqqūm tree?
translations.63: Indeed We have made it a punishment for the wrongdoers.
translations.64: Indeed it is a tree that emerges from the depths of hell.
translations.65: Its spathes are as if they were devils' heads.<{["F", 1]}>
translations.66: Indeed they will eat from it and gorge with it their bellies.
translations.67: Indeed, on top of that they will take a solution of scalding water.
translations.68: Then indeed their retreat will be toward hell.
translations.69: Indeed they had found their fathers astray,
translations.70: yet they press on in their footsteps.
translations.71: Certainly most of the ancients went astray before them,
translations.72: and certainly We had sent warners among them.
translations.73: So _observe_ how was the fate of those who were warned
translations.75: Certainly Noah called out to Us, and how well We responded!
translations.76: We delivered him and his family from the great agony,
translations.77: and made his descendants the survivors,
translations.78: and left for him a good name among posterity:
translations.80: Thus indeed do We reward the virtuous.
translations.81: He is indeed one of Our faithful servants.
translations.83: Indeed Abraham was among his followers,
translations.84: when he came to his Lord with a sound heart,<{["F", 1]}>
translations.85: when he said to his father and his people, 'What is it that you are worshiping?
translations.86: Is it a lie, gods other than Allah, that you desire?
translations.87: Then what is your idea about the Lord of all the worlds?'
translations.88: Then he made an observation of the stars<{["F", 1]}>
translations.90: So they went away leaving him behind.
translations.91: Then he stole away to their gods and said, 'Will you not eat?
translations.93: Then he attacked them, striking forcefully.
translations.95: He said, 'Do you worship what you have yourselves carved,
translations.96: when Allah has created you and whatever you make?'
translations.97: They said, 'Build a structure for him and cast him into a huge fire.'
translations.98: So they sought to outwit him, but We made them the lowermost.
translations.99: He said, 'Indeed I am going toward my Lord, who will guide me.'
translations.100: 'My Lord! Give me [an heir], one of the righteous.'
translations.101: So We gave him the good news of a forbearing son.<{["F", 1]}>
translations.102: When he was old enough to assist in his endeavour, he said, 'My son! I see in a dream that I am sacrificing you. See what you think.' He said, 'Father! Do whatever you have been commanded. If Allah wishes, you will find me to be patient.'
translations.103: So when they had both submitted [to Allah's will], and he had laid him down on his forehead,
translations.104: We called out to him, 'O Abraham!
translations.105: You have indeed fulfilled the vision!<{["F", 1]}> Thus indeed do We reward the virtuous!
translations.106: This was indeed a manifest test.'
translations.107: Then We ransomed him with a great sacrifice,
translations.108: and left for him a good name in posterity:
translations.110: Thus do We reward the virtuous.
translations.111: He is indeed one of Our faithful servants.
translations.112: And We gave him the good news of [the birth of] Isaac, a prophet, one of the righteous.
translations.113: And We blessed him and Isaac. Among their descendants [some] are virtuous, and [some] who manifestly wrong themselves.
translations.114: Certainly We favoured Moses and Aaron,
translations.115: and delivered them and their people from the great agony,
translations.116: and We helped them so that they became the victors.
translations.117: We gave them the illuminating scripture
translations.118: and guided them to the straight path,
translations.119: and left for them a good name in posterity.
translations.121: Thus indeed do We reward the virtuous.
translations.122: They are indeed among Our faithful servants.
translations.123: And indeed Ilyās was one of the apostles,
translations.124: when he said to his people, 'Will you not be Godwary?
translations.125: Do you invoke Baal and abandon the best of creators,
translations.126: Allah, your Lord and Lord of your forefathers?'
translations.127: But they impugned him. So they will indeed be arraigned [before Him]
translations.129: We left for him a good name in posterity.
translations.131: Thus indeed do We reward the virtuous.
translations.132: He is indeed one of Our faithful servants.
translations.133: And indeed Lot was one of the apostles,
translations.134: when We delivered him and all his family,
translations.135: except an old woman among those who remained behind.
translations.137: And indeed you pass by them at dawn
translations.138: and at night. So do you not apply reason?
translations.139: And indeed Jonah was one of the apostles,
translations.140: when he absconded toward the laden ship.
translations.141: Then he drew lots with them and he was the one to be refuted.
translations.142: Then the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy.
translations.143: And had he not been one of those who celebrate Allah's glory,
translations.144: he would have surely remained in its belly till the day they will be resurrected.
translations.145: Then We cast him on a bare shore, and he was sick.
translations.146: So We made a gourd plant grow above him.
translations.147: We sent him to a [community of] hundred thousand or more,
translations.148: and they believed [in him]. So We provided for them for a while.
translations.149: _Ask_ them, are daughters to be for _your_ Lord while sons are to be for them?<{["F", 1]}>
translations.150: Did We create the angels females while they were present?<{["F", 1]}>
translations.151: Look! It is indeed out of their mendacity that they say,
translations.152: 'Allah has begotten,' and they indeed speak a falsehood.
translations.153: Has he preferred daughters to sons?
translations.154: What is the matter with you? How do you judge?
translations.155: Will you not then take admonition?
translations.156: Do you have a manifest authority?<{["F", 1]}>
translations.157: Then produce your scripture, should you be truthful.
translations.158: And they have set up a kinship between Him and the jinn, while the jinn certainly know that they will indeed be presented [before Him].
translations.159: Clear is Allah of whatever they allege [about Him],
translations.161: Indeed you and what you worship
translations.163: except someone who is bound for hell.
translations.164: 'There is none among us but has a known place.<{["F", 1]}>
translations.165: Indeed it is we who are the ranged ones.
translations.166: Indeed it is we who are those who celebrate Allah's glory.'
translations.168: 'Had we possessed a reminder from the ancients,
translations.169: we would surely have been Allah's exclusive servants.'
translations.170: But they disbelieved it [when it came to them]. Soon they will know.
translations.171: Certainly Our decree has gone beforehand in favour of Our servants, the apostles,
translations.172: that they will indeed receive [Allah's] help,
translations.173: and indeed Our hosts will be the victors.
translations.174: So _leave_ them alone for a while,
translations.175: and _watch_ them; soon they will see [the truth of the matter].
translations.176: Do they seek to hasten Our punishment?
translations.177: But when it descends in their courtyard it will be a dismal dawn for those who had been warned.
translations.178: So _leave_ them alone for a while,
translations.180: Clear is your Lord, the Lord of Might, of whatever they allege [concerning Him].
translations.182: All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of all the worlds.
